He was naturally in fear of the party to which he had once belonged himself; but he expresses no apprehension of the Judaising Christians, as might have been expected had their antagonism really been as violent as some make out. Robertson notes that Paul foresaw trouble all the way to Jerusalem.

themes: that I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea
that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints
that I may come unto you with joy by the will of God

33.pericope_label: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen

schools.summary: Gill sets the last title beside the other two of the chapter. God has been styled the God of patience and the God of hope for his concern in those graces, and he is here styled the God of peace for his concern in that peace which is made between him and his people by the blood of Christ. That peace was first upon his thoughts, which are therefore called thoughts of peace; a council of peace was held between him and his Son, in which the scheme of reconciliation was drawn; he entered into a covenant of peace with Christ, which takes its very name from that article; and he appointed Christ the peacemaker. He is besides the giver of all true and solid peace of conscience, the peace of God which passeth the understanding of natural men, and which, when he gives it, none can trouble.

Clarke says the object of the epistle is to establish peace between believing Jews and Gentiles and to show them their mutual obligations, so that it closes with a prayer that the God from whom peace comes and by whom it is preserved may be for ever with them; but he holds that the Amen does not appear to have been written by the apostle, being wanting in some of the most ancient manuscripts. He ends the chapter with a plea for forbearance. Each side has been ready to take out of the fourteenth and fifteenth chapters such expressions as seemed suitable to its own case, but few have been found who have taken up the whole. If you dispute concerning any doctrine, Clarke says, let it be to find out truth and not to support a preconceived opinion; avoid all polemical heat and rancour, which prove the absence of the religion of Christ, for whatever does not lead you to love God and man more is most assuredly from beneath. He closes with a verse of the pious Mr Herbert: be calm in arguing, for fierceness makes error a fault and truth discourtesy; why should I feel another man's mistakes more than his sickness or his poverty? In love I should; but anger is not love, nor wisdom neither — therefore gently move.

Barnes takes the benediction as asking the very thing the whole letter has laboured at, that the God who gives peace would impart union of sentiment and feeling, particularly between the Jewish and the Gentile Christians. He looks back over the chapter's prayers and finds them answered in an unlooked-for way. His main desire was granted, for he was permitted to visit Rome; yet the very thing from which he sought deliverance, the opposition of the Jews, made it necessary for him to appeal to Caesar, and that appeal was the means of accomplishing his desire. God thus often grants our main desire, but may make use of the very thing we pray to be delivered from as the means of fulfilling the request. It is right to express our desires, all our desires, to God, but with a willingness that he choose his own means to accomplish them. Ellicott holds that the weight of manuscript authority is decidedly for retaining the closing word, though three of some importance omit it, and that it does not follow that the benediction was intended to close the epistle, since intercalated benedictions and doxologies are frequent in Paul. Robertson reports the conclusion drawn further: because of the Amen some scholars would make this the close of the epistle and the sixteenth chapter a separate letter to the Ephesians, but the manuscripts are against it, and there is nothing strange in Paul's having so many friends at Rome though he had never been there, since Rome was the centre of the world's life, and all men sooner or later hoped to see it.
